metadata.title: Ramanujan and exponent-pair budget
metadata.claim_status: Exact identities and exponent algebra; compatibility audit only.

plain_language.result: The retained 15/32 clustered core and 1/4 wing are compatible with classical tools. The remaining conservative primitive obstacle is the shallow/terminal boundary-layer mass.

ramanujan.key_correlation: A large divisor contribution r requires r|n, so large arithmetic coefficients occur only at proportionally larger dual frequencies.

core_Q_le_R.decision: The 15/32 clustering barrier disappears at exponent-budget level.

wing_Q_gt_R.decision: The 1/4 wing has polylog(B)*S0^(-1) relative saving.

weighted_sum.divisor_weights: Fixed moments of 2^omega and tau cost only powers of log B after lambda_1-weighted harmonic summation.
weighted_sum.retained_error: polylog(B)*exp(-c*sqrt(log B)), hence smaller than every fixed negative power of log B.

boundary_layers.problem: They are o(B log^4 B), but exceed the conservative raw target B*(log B)^(2-eta) needed before absolute global Mobius inversion.

incompatibility.conclusion: Those requirements destroy growth of the short side. The boundary layers must be evaluated, not discarded.

literature: Trudgian-Yang, Toward optimal exponent pairs, arXiv:2306.05599
Pliego, Estimates for a three-dimensional exponential sum with monomials, arXiv:2211.02096
Chan-Kumchev, On sums of Ramanujan sums, arXiv:1009.4432

closed: retained deep/small-d discrepancy at the conservative primitive scale
not_closed: full raw polynomial expansion or Mobius-coupled boundary treatment
decision.next_stage: 12-N1-2j: restore shallow and terminal layers using floor-first summation, Mellin/Perron separation, or Mobius inversion before truncation.

not_claimed: A proved raw or primitive asymptotic.
That Ramanujan second moments alone suffice.
Final constants or complete endpoint bookkeeping.
